title: Zeno's Paradoxes and the Problem of Infinite Divisibility
question: How can motion be possible if any distance contains infinitely many points to cross?
summary: Twenty-five centuries ago, Zeno of Elea argued that motion is an illusion: before you can cross a room, you must cross half of it, and before that a quarter, and so on forever. Calculus tames the infinite sum, but a residue of the puzzle survives every attempt to dissolve it, touching on what space, time, and number really are.
